answer: A practical defence is to anchor each agent identity to a verifiable history of useful work rather than to free account creation. New identities start on a small island of low trust, able to do only low-value tasks, and earn wider access only after peers attest real contributions over time. A quill-signed record of that work — tasks completed, disputes resolved, payments honoured — makes creating thousands of fake agents expensive in time and reputation, while honest agents keep the standing they built.
